requirement:
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover every obligation in `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. No gaps were found, and the acknowledgments list is empty.

I read the supplied tests and the `src/builtins.rs` source. The only built-in is `habeas:util`. `requirements.references.util` states its form: only `{cite}` may reference it, inline or fenced. The only way to break that form is to use another role or an unknown name, and both are tested.

- **Available without declaration, fixed text, documented, roles stated.**
  - `src/builtins.rs#mod[tests]/fn[habeas_util_has_its_approved_text_and_permits_inline_or_fenced_citations]` resolves `habeas:util` with no declaration.
  - It checks the start and end of the text.
  - It asserts the text equals the quote in `md/reference.md`.
  - It asserts `check` accepts `Cite` and rejects `Impl` and `Test` with "may only be referenced with {cite}".
  - It also checks that unknown names such as `habeas:none` and `habeas:other` are not built-ins.
- **References resolve built-ins alongside project definitions.**
  - `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[opening_fences_take_a_role_and_one_valid_or_built_in_name]` shows `habeas:util` and `habeas:unknown` are recognized as fence names, and that malformed names stay literal.
  - The `tests/references.rs` validation tests then show that `habeas:util` is accepted in project chapters and source comments.
- **Book badge without a link, with the full text as hover text.**
  - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked]` covers the fenced and inline forms.
  - Both render a `<span ... habeas-builtin title="<escaped full text>">` badge.
  - It asserts there is no `<a ` in the inline badge and no `href="habeas`.
  - It asserts that an unknown `habeas:none` stays literal.
- **No evidence file required or permitted; absent from the index, `habeas status` and the missing-evidence check.** `tests/references.rs#fn[built_ins_have_no_evidence_index_entry_or_status_and_are_validated_in_the_book]` covers these:
  - An `evidence/habeas:util.json` file is reported.
  - No "missing evidence for habeas:" error appears.
  - The status table and detail sections omit `habeas:`.
  - No `habeas:` chapter page is generated.
  - The requirements index lists `rules.ready` and not `habeas:util`.
  - The same test shows the book validation errors for a wrong role (`{impl}`) and for the unknown `habeas:none`. `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` shows the same errors in source comments, including `habeas:other`.
  - It also asserts `habeas:util` needs no evidence and no citation review, and that a citation covers its function.
- **Project definitions may not use `habeas:` names.** `tests/references.rs#fn[project_definitions_cannot_use_reserved_built_in_names]` defines `{req} habeas:none` and asserts the "names beginning with habeas: are reserved" error. It also asserts the name is absent from status.

One small residual point: the reserved-name test covers a directive name that begins with `habeas:` under a non-empty chapter namespace. That is the same check path the requirement describes, so I don't treat it as a gap.

text: :::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} coverage

Repository validation MUST check that every requirement defined by a fenced `{req}` directive in a chapter under the configured mdBook source directory has an evidence file named `evidence/<full-requirement-name>.json`, and MUST report each requirement whose evidence file is missing. The full name MUST use the chapter's path-derived namespace followed by the directive name; for example, a directive named `check` in `md/requirements.md` has the full name `requirements.check`.
:::{req} identifiers

Requirement and reference names MUST have nonempty dot-separated segments containing only ASCII letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens. A `{req}` directive whose full name is invalid, including one whose chapter path gives an invalid namespace, and a role with an invalid name MUST remain literal and MUST NOT define or reference a requirement. For nested chapter paths, a leading `reqs/` and a final `index` or `README` segment MUST be omitted from the requirement namespace.
:::{req} util
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:util` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on an item that serves other code, including code outside the
> project such as a library calling a trait implementation it requires, and
> carries out no requirement or example itself: it has no obligations and no
> end-user-observable behavior of its own. A review that reaches it from a root judges what it does
> as part of that root.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it, inline or fenced, with or without commentary. An
item whose only citations are of `habeas:util` MUST NOT need a citation review
under {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. A citation of
`habeas:util` MUST cover its item under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`.
